english.title: Incite another to corruptly solicit / receive a gift / loan / fee / advantage
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) incited **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON(S) OR 'ANOTHER'..) to corruptly solicit, receive or agree to receive a gift, loan, fee, reward, or advantage, namely **(..SPECIFY..), as an inducement to or reward for or otherwise on account of any member, officer, or servant of a public body, namely **(..SPECIFY THE BODY..), doing or forbearing to do something in respect of a matter or transaction actual or proposed, in which the public body was concerned, namely **(..SPECIFY THE MATTER OR TRANSACTION..)

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
This offence wording is now OBSOLETE repealed by the Serious Crime Act 2007.

Now see offences of intentionally encouraging or assisting an offence (section 44); encouraging or assisting an offence believing it will be committed (section 45) and encouraging or assisting offences believing one or more will be committed (section 46) of the Serious Crime Act 2007.

(i) See also the presumption of corruption provided by section 2 of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1916.
(ii) In R v Natji (Times 14.3.02) it was decided that "Public body" (under this Act) did NOT include a government department and/or the Crown, but see the Prevention of Corruption Act 1906 which widened the definition.
